assessment.summary: EGFR (P00533) is one of the most extensively validated and drugged targets in oncology, with 393 PDB structures (best resolution 1.07Å), 26,600 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and 20 approved drugs including small molecules and biologics. The structural, chemical, and literature evidence collectively place this target in the highest tier of druggability with exceptional confidence across all dimensions.
evidence_gaps: Median IC50 of 2000 nM across all ChEMBL entries suggests a large proportion of the chemical space is weakly active or non-selective compounds, which may reflect broad screening campaigns rather than a potency concern per se

AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 75.9 with only 70.7% high-confidence residues suggests disordered regions (likely extracellular or linker domains) not well-captured structurally, though the kinase domain is well-resolved by X-ray

Resistance mechanisms (e.g., T790M, C797S, exon 20 insertions) limit clinical utility of existing drugs in certain patient subpopulations — next-generation inhibitor coverage of all resistance variants is incomplete
Some approved drugs listed may reflect combination approvals or salt forms rather than entirely distinct chemical entities, warranting careful deduplication
Glioblastoma/CNS indications remain challenging due to blood-brain barrier penetration, and efficacy data in these settings is limited despite high EGFR expression
